title: Sprint deploy tooling smoke-sheet & release narrative (Mar 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact deploy tooling smoke-sheet and human-readable release narrative for the sprint-level release window. Intended for the 24h preflight -> launch -> 48h stabilization lifecycle. Keep this page open during handoffs; it contains the quick checks, expected signals, and short-form release notes we ship to stakeholders.

Status: draft. This is intentionally terse — copy into the official release notes page once we confirm post-launch telemetry.

Summary narrative (one paragraph):
We are rolling out the v2 batching/kv-cache optimization to the hosted-api pool and Dedicated staging lanes. Goal: 15–25% token-cost reduction for common chat workloads and ~5–10% median latency improvement at p50 for 1–2s tails. Canary to 2% traffic -> ramp to 25% over 4 hours -> full by 48h if no regressions. Canary includes a small model-variant fallback (quantized fallback) and prefix-caching enabled for routes /chat and /generate.

Day-by-day rollout calendar (compact):
- T-48h (Mar 18): Final smoke run in staging, export baseline traces, notify CS + Sales (minimal).
- T-24h (Mar 19 morning): Lock release notes, enable canary toggle, start warmup script for batchers.
- T-0 (Mar 19 14:00 PDT): Flip canary -> 2% traffic. Watch first 15m p95 and error rate.
- T+1h: If green, ramp to 10% traffic.
- T+4h: If green, ramp to 25% traffic and begin telemetry drift checks.
- T+24h: Evaluate quality regressions vs evaluation set and prompt CI.
- T+48h: Final decision to open to 100% or rollback. Postmortem lock opens if any critical signal triggered.

Quick owner map (primary -> backup):
- Release lead: Aisha Patel -> Marco Silva
- Serving runtime lead: Dana Klein -> Ravi Menon
- Observability / telemetry: Marco Silva -> SRE on-call
- Rollback executor (infra): Ravi Menon -> release-oncall
- Customer comms owner: Priya Desai (CS)
- Stakeholder updates: automated at +1h, +4h, +24h via #release-signals

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-24h):
- [ ] All commits merged to release branch and tagged (git tag: release/sprint-2026-03)
- [ ] Smoke tests in staging passed (smoke id: smoke/2026-03-19-01)
- [ ] Load warmup completed for batcher pools (script: infra/scripts/warmup-batcher.sh)
- [ ] Canary config validated on dedicated pool (canary-config-id: canary-2026-03-v2)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards cloned and baseline run stored (dash: /d/launch/2026-03-v2)
- [ ] SLAs and quota knobs reviewed with product (noted exceptions documented)
- [ ] Rollback artifact builds available and validated (artifact id: rollback/v1-to-v0-2026-03)
- [ ] CS comms draft ready for first +4h update

Launch quick checks (first 30 minutes):
- Check 0m: all canary pods healthy (kubectl get pods -l app=serving-canary)
- Check 5m: error-rate < 0.5% above baseline (compare to baseline window last 24h)
- Check 15m: p95 latency not worse than +20% over baseline; p50 within expected target
- Check 30m: token cost per request trending downwards for sample routes
- Check 30m: sampling evaluation (3 prompts) show no hallucination increase; screenshot and attach to the release thread

Telemetry KPIs and thresholds (alerts):
- Error spike: >0.5% absolute increase in 15m window -> trigger paging
- Latency tail: p95 increase >20% relative to baseline -> page
- Quality regression: automated eval delta >2 points (prompt-CI) -> create quick fix ticket
- Cost delta: expected token-cost reduction target not met at 24h -> note in release digest and investigate

Rollback plan (fast rollback):
- Trigger: any paged alert or sustained (>30m) p95 degradation >30%
- Action: switch routing policy to model-variant fallback (roll route to fallback-id: q-fallback-2026-03)
- If routing change insufficient: deploy rollback artifact (infra/deploy rollback/v1) and set traffic back to 100% previous variant
- Post-rollback: capture traces for the 30m before and after, start incident timeline doc, and notify stakeholders

Release notes draft (bulleted; will be extended for external-facing changelog):
- Feature: v2 batching + prefix KV-cache — reduced per-token CPU and higher packing efficiency for chat workloads
- Improvement: median latency improvements on short-chat prompts (expected p50: -5–10%)
- Risk: minor quality delta observed in a subset of prompts under heavy batching; fallback enabled as mitigation
- Migration: no client changes required; internal route flag controls behavior

Known issues / caveats (to surface during +4h update):
- Intermittent tokenization mismatch on locale-specific prompts (observed in ~0.03% of sampled calls) — hotfix branch prepared
- Autoscaler edge-case: instance churn when batcher warmup overlaps with scale-up; we have a throttle patch staged
- Observability: some traces are dropped when prefix cache is cold — we plan retention increase for first 48h

Operational reminders / commands:
- Quick rollback routing: infra/scripts/route-switch --to q-fallback-2026-03
- Canary scale check: k9s / cluster -> nodes -> filter serving-canary
- Collect baseline traces: scripts/telemetry/export_baseline.sh --tag release-2026-03

Post-launch 24h checklist:
- [ ] Automated prompt-CI run and manual spot-check complete
- [ ] CS update at +24h with incident summary (if any)
- [ ] Cost analysis preliminary comment (finance contact: Lena Ortiz)
- [ ] Decide full open or staggered extension to remaining regions

48h post-launch mini-retro (notes to self):
- What went well: warmup reduced initial p95 spikes; fallback routing worked without manual intervention
- Friction: rollout didn't include an easy way to surface per-route batch sizes in the dashboard — flag for product
- Follow-ups: create infra ticket to add batch-size gauge; add extra prompt set for locale tokenization test

Open questions (unresolved, tag before finalizing notes):
- Do we want the cost-savings baseline to be the last-7d median or the 30d trend? (affects percent reduction claims)
- Should we include the quantized fallback in the public changelog, or only mention as internal mitigation?

Appendix / links (quick):
- Launch thread: https://slack.redwood-inference.com/archives/CRELEASES/p1654321
- Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/d/launch/2026-03-v2
- Prompt-CI run: https://ci.redwood-inference/prompt-ci/2026-03-19

Notes to reviewers: copy any fixes into the canonical release notes doc at CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-2026-03 before closing the loop. If you are on-call during launch, please paste your checks here as lines prefixed by your name so we can track sequence.

---
Small scratch area (todo lines and quick thoughts):
- Marco: validate batcher warmup time on small GPU types (T4)
- Dana: confirm fallback quantization bit-widths and perf profile attach
- Ravi: ensure rollback image has same health probe config
- Aisha: draft first +4h status update (short bullets, one-sentence impact)

End of doc.
